replies.body: Hi Alex — this is actually on our roadmap for Q1, so your timing is good. Can you send pricing for two sites to start (Reno and our Columbus DC)? Please loop in Marcus Chen, he runs the Reno facility and would own the pilot. We're targeting a go-live before peak season next year. Best, Dana

expected_extraction.next_step: Send pricing for two sites (Reno and Columbus) and loop in Marcus Chen
expected_extraction.timeline: Q1 planning; go-live before peak season next year

replies.subject: Re: Cutting pick labor at your Reno DC

replies.body: Alex, I can do 30 minutes next Tuesday or Thursday morning. We run about 240,000 sq ft in Memphis and labor is our number one headache right now — we're paying $21/hr and still can't staff second shift. Send me a calendar invite and whatever one-pager you have on deployment timelines. — Tom

expected_extraction.next_step: Send calendar invite for Tuesday or Thursday morning plus one-pager on deployment timelines
expected_extraction.pain_point: Labor cost and staffing — $21/hr and still cannot staff second shift
expected_extraction.timeline: Call next Tuesday or Thursday morning

replies.subject: Re: Labor costs at your Memphis facility

replies.body: Interesting. We're a food distribution DC so everything has to work at -10°F in the freezer zone — do your pallet movers actually operate at that temperature, or is this ambient-only? If they do, I'd look at a case study from another cold storage operator. Thanks, Priya

expected_extraction.next_step: Confirm freezer-temperature operation and send a cold storage case study
expected_extraction.pain_point: Needs automation that works in -10°F freezer zones

replies.subject: Re: Automation for cold storage picking

replies.body: We're drowning during peak — last November we were 40% over planned labor hours two weeks in a row. Not ready to talk contracts or anything, but send me the overview deck and I'll read it over the weekend. Greg

expected_extraction.next_step: Send overview deck
expected_extraction.pain_point: Peak season throughput — 40% over planned labor hours last November

replies.subject: Re: Peak season throughput

replies.body: Alex, the product fits what we're trying to do, but your pricing came in well above the number I can defend internally. Our automation envelope for next year is roughly $400–500K across all projects, and your quote eats most of it for one site. If there's a phased option or a lease model, I'd look again. Sandra

expected_extraction.budget_signal: $400–500K total automation budget for next year across all projects
expected_extraction.next_step: Respond with phased deployment or lease/RaaS pricing option

replies.subject: Re: Goods-to-person for pharma DCs

replies.body: Too expensive for us right now, plain and simple. We're a single-site operation and the payback math doesn't work at our volume. Maybe for the big 3PLs this pencils out, but not here. — Mike

expected_extraction.next_step: Send ROI calculator or low-volume case study; otherwise nurture
expected_extraction.pain_point: ROI/payback does not work at single-site volume

replies.subject: Re: Pallet movers for your Atlanta DC

replies.body: We signed a three-year agreement with Symbotic last spring, so our automation roadmap is locked for the foreseeable future. That said, our sister facility in Portland is evaluating options for 2027 and you'd want to talk to Rachel Nguyen, their Ops VP — she asked me about goods-to-person vendors just last month. Karen

expected_extraction.next_step: Thank Karen and open a new thread with Rachel Nguyen about the Portland 2027 evaluation
expected_extraction.referral: Rachel Nguyen, Ops VP, Portland sister facility
expected_extraction.timeline: Incumbent contract runs three years from last spring; Portland facility evaluating for 2027

label.edge_case_note: Both an objection (locked into competitor Symbotic for three years) AND a warm referral to Rachel Nguyen at the Portland sister facility — classifier must surface the referral, not just file it as a lost objection.

replies.subject: Re: Your automation rollout

replies.body: We already run Geek+ robots across four of our six sites and the integration with our WMS took the better part of a year. Not looking to rip and replace. If you ever support mixed fleets in the same building, that conversation I'd take. James

expected_extraction.next_step: Nurture; re-engage if/when mixed-fleet support ships
expected_extraction.pain_point: Incumbent Geek+ fleet in 4 of 6 sites; long WMS integration

replies.subject: Re: Throughput at scale

replies.body: Not this quarter. We're mid-implementation on a new WMS and my team has zero bandwidth for another project until that settles. Check back with me in January and I'll give you a straight answer either way. Alicia

expected_extraction.next_step: Schedule follow-up for January
expected_extraction.pain_point: Team bandwidth — mid-implementation on a new WMS

replies.subject: Re: Automation timing

replies.body: Hi Alex, appreciate you reaching out. We're a small operation — 38,000 sq ft, one shift — and everything's running smoothly enough right now that I can't justify looking at automation this year. No hard feelings, it's just not a priority for 2026. Best of luck, Robert

expected_extraction.next_step: Polite close; long-term nurture only

replies.subject: Re: Your email on pallet automation

replies.body: Hi, you've reached the wrong person — I work in HR, not operations. Warehouse automation decisions sit with our Director of Operations, Dan Whitaker, at the Joliet facility. You'll want to reach out to him directly. Heather

expected_extraction.next_step: Redirect outreach to Dan Whitaker
expected_extraction.referral: Dan Whitaker, Director of Operations, Joliet facility

replies.subject: Re: Warehouse automation inquiry

replies.body: Wrong guy. I keep the forklifts running, I don't buy robots. That'd be corporate in Detroit. Steve

expected_extraction.next_step: Find the corporate operations contact in Detroit
expected_extraction.referral: Corporate office in Detroit (no named contact)

replies.subject: Re: Automation

replies.body: I am out of the office at our annual operations summit and will return on Monday, November 2, with limited access to email until then. If your matter is urgent, please contact my colleague Jordan Ellis, who is covering operations decisions in my absence, at j.ellis@summitridge.example. Otherwise I will reply when I return. — Melissa Grant, VP of Operations

expected_extraction.next_step: Contact delegate Jordan Ellis now; re-engage Melissa after November 2
expected_extraction.referral: Jordan Ellis, colleague covering operations decisions, j.ellis@summitridge.example

label.edge_case_note: Out-of-office that contains BOTH a return date (Monday, November 2) AND a named delegate (Jordan Ellis) — correct handling is to route to the delegate now and re-engage Melissa after Nov 2, not to drop the lead.

replies.subject: Out of office: Re: Deployment timelines

replies.body: Thank you for your email. I am currently on parental leave and will not be reading messages regularly. I expect to be back in the office in early December. For anything time-sensitive, please contact the operations desk at ops@pacificrim.example.

expected_extraction.next_step: Pause outreach until early December or contact the operations desk

replies.subject: Automatic reply: Re: Your DC automation

replies.body: Can we talk this week? Our board approved a $750K automation budget in September and the one condition is that whatever we pick has to be live before the holiday ramp — so installation by end of October next year at the latest. If your deployment timeline can't hit that, tell me now and save us both the meeting. Nancy

expected_extraction.budget_signal: $750K automation budget approved by the board in September
expected_extraction.next_step: Confirm deployment can hit end-of-October install, then book a call this week
expected_extraction.timeline: Must be installed by end of October next year; talk this week

replies.subject: Re: Scaling for holiday volume

replies.body: Send me the deck and the ROI model you mentioned. Our labor costs went up 18% this year and finance is asking every department for a plan, so this will get read. Can't promise more than that right now. Chris

expected_extraction.next_step: Send deck and ROI model
expected_extraction.pain_point: Labor costs up 18% this year; finance demanding a plan

replies.subject: Re: Labor savings estimate

replies.body: Bad timing, Alex. We're breaking ground on a 120,000 sq ft expansion in March and the building won't be ready until Q4. Automation decisions happen once we're in the new space, not before. If you want to talk specs for the new building, that conversation starts around September. Paul

expected_extraction.next_step: Schedule re-engagement for September to discuss specs for the new building
expected_extraction.timeline: Expansion breaks ground in March, ready Q4; specs conversation starts around September

replies.subject: Re: Timing on automation

replies.body: This is the third email from your company this month. Remove me from your list — I don't want to receive these anymore. Kevin

expected_extraction.next_step: Suppress contact immediately; do not reply with a pitch

replies.subject: Re: Northwind Robotics outreach

replies.body: Hola Alex, gracias por escribir. Estamos evaluando opciones de automatización para nuestro centro en Guadalajara, sobre todo porque nos cuesta mucho contratar personal para el turno nocturno. ¿Podrías enviarme información sobre costos y tiempos de implementación? Saludos, María Fernanda

expected_extraction.next_step: Enviar información de costos y tiempos de implementación, en español
expected_extraction.pain_point: Dificultad para contratar personal para el turno nocturno (night-shift staffing)

replies.subject: Re: Automatización para su centro de distribución

replies.body: Alex, me interesa avanzar. Tenemos tres centros de distribución y el piloto sería en Bogotá, con la idea de estar operativos antes de la temporada alta de fin de año. ¿Podemos tener una llamada el jueves o el viernes para revisar la propuesta técnica y los precios por sitio? Carlos

expected_extraction.next_step: Agendar llamada el jueves o viernes para revisar propuesta técnica y precios por sitio
expected_extraction.timeline: Operativo antes de la temporada alta de fin de año; llamada el jueves o viernes

replies.subject: Re: Robots para su almacén en Bogotá

replies.body: El producto nos encaja, pero el precio está fuera de nuestro presupuesto para este año. Nuestro tope para proyectos de almacén es de unos 250.000 dólares y su cotización lo duplica. Si hubiera una opción de pago por uso o en cuotas, podríamos reconsiderarlo el próximo trimestre. Lucía

expected_extraction.budget_signal: Tope de unos $250,000 para proyectos de almacén; la cotización lo duplica
expected_extraction.next_step: Ofrecer opción de pago por uso o en cuotas y retomar el próximo trimestre

replies.subject: Re: Su consulta sobre automatización

replies.body: Gracias por el contacto. El año pasado firmamos un contrato de cinco años con Dematic para la automatización de nuestros dos centros principales, así que no estamos en el mercado por ahora. Cuando ese contrato se acerque a su fin, con gusto conversamos. Jorge

expected_extraction.next_step: Nurture a largo plazo; retomar cuando el contrato con Dematic se acerque a su fin
expected_extraction.timeline: Contrato vigente de cinco años firmado el año pasado con Dematic

replies.subject: Re: Automatización de almacenes

replies.body: Hola, por ahora no. Estamos en plena mudanza a una nave más grande y el equipo no puede evaluar nada nuevo hasta que terminemos de instalarnos, probablemente en febrero. Si me escribes entonces, lo revisamos con calma. Ana Paula

expected_extraction.next_step: Programar seguimiento para febrero
expected_extraction.pain_point: Sin capacidad durante la mudanza a una nave más grande
expected_extraction.timeline: Re-evaluar en febrero, tras la mudanza

replies.subject: Re: Información sobre robots móviles

replies.body: Creo que escribió a la persona equivocada. Yo estoy en compras de materiales indirectos; las decisiones de automatización del almacén las lleva la gerencia de operaciones. La persona indicada es Verónica Campos, nuestra gerente de operaciones. Ricardo

expected_extraction.next_step: Redirigir el contacto a Verónica Campos

replies.subject: Re: Su correo sobre robots para almacén

replies.body: Alex，你好。我们在苏州的配送中心面积约8万平方米，最近人工成本涨得很快，旺季经常招不到人。我对你们的托盘搬运机器人比较感兴趣，能否先发一份产品资料和大致的报价范围？另外想了解一下，从签约到正式上线一般需要多久。王建国

expected_extraction.next_step: 发送产品资料和大致报价范围，并说明签约到上线的周期
expected_extraction.pain_point: 人工成本上涨，旺季招不到人（苏州配送中心约8万平方米）

replies.subject: 回复：关于仓库自动化方案

replies.body: Alex，你好。这个方向我们今年已经立项了，预算大约180万元，先在成都的一个仓试点，计划明年3月前上线。我周四下午有空，可以开个视频会议，请把你们的技术方案和类似食品行业的案例提前发我看一下。李晓梅

expected_extraction.next_step: 约周四下午视频会议，提前发送技术方案和食品行业案例
expected_extraction.timeline: 计划明年3月前上线；周四下午视频会议

replies.subject: 回复：货到人机器人试点项目

replies.body: Alex，你好。你们的方案我看过，方向没问题，但时间上实在不合适。我们仓库刚签了三年的租约，明年还要做GSP合规改造，改造期间不可能同时上自动化项目。等合规改造结束、大概后年年初，我们再认真评估比较合适。张伟

expected_extraction.next_step: 后年年初再跟进评估
expected_extraction.pain_point: 合规改造期间无法并行自动化项目
expected_extraction.timeline: 明年GSP合规改造；后年年初再评估

replies.subject: 回复：自动化改造的时间

replies.body: 您好，我是陈静。我目前正在休年假，将于11月9日（周一）返回办公室，休假期间无法及时查看邮件。如有紧急事项，请联系我的同事刘洋，他负责我休假期间的运营事务，邮箱为 liuyang@lanjing.example。我返回后会尽快回复您的邮件。陈静

expected_extraction.next_step: 紧急事项联系刘洋；否则11月9日后再跟进陈静

replies.subject: 自动回复：回复：仓库机器人咨询

replies.body: Alex，你好。先问一个技术问题：我们的仓库用的是用友的WMS系统，你们的机器人调度系统能和用友WMS对接吗？另外，巷道宽度只有2.8米，你们的托盘搬运机器人能正常通行和转弯吗？这两个问题确认了，我们再往下谈。刘海峰

expected_extraction.next_step: 回复WMS对接能力与2.8米巷道的通行/转弯规格，再继续推进
expected_extraction.pain_point: 需要与用友WMS对接；巷道宽度仅2.8米

replies.subject: 回复：请教一个技术问题

replies.body: Alex，谢谢你的邮件，方案写得很认真。说实话我们今年实在排不开了，预算和人力都压在新仓建设上，现在真不是谈这个的时候。不过我把你的资料留下了，等这一阵忙完、明年一季度预算出来之后，说不定我们会重新考虑。到时候再联系吧。赵明轩

expected_extraction.next_step: 标记为 not-now，明年一季度预算发布后重新联系
expected_extraction.pain_point: 预算和人力都压在新仓建设上
expected_extraction.timeline: 明年一季度预算出来之后可能重新考虑

label.edge_case_note: 表面上是礼貌拒绝（"现在真不是谈这个的时候"），实质是"不是这个季度"——明年一季度预算出来后可能重新考虑。应标为 not-now 并设置明年Q1跟进，而不是当作永久拒绝丢弃。
